questions: Did this problem begin gradually rather than suddenly?
Has the leaning of your trunk progressively worsened over time?
Does your trunk become noticeably straighter when you lie down or when someone passively straightens you?
Do you have slowness in everyday movements, such as dressing, turning in bed, or getting up from a chair?
Does your left side feel stiff or rigid?
Have you noticed a tremor when your hand is relaxed?
Do you have difficulty taking the first step or experience episodes in which your feet feel stuck to the floor?
Have your steps become shorter or more shuffling?
Have you had any falls or near-falls?
Has your handwriting become smaller than it used to be?
Has your voice become softer or more monotonous?
Have other people noticed that your facial expressions have become reduced?
Have you experienced reduced sense of smell?
Do you act out your dreams by talking, shouting, or moving in your sleep?
Have you had constipation that began before these movement problems?
Have you experienced dizziness when standing, urinary problems, or erectile difficulties?
Have you noticed memory problems, visual hallucinations, or marked fluctuations in alertness?
Have you had painful back or hip problems that could force you to lean to one side?
Do you have weakness, numbness, or altered sensation in either arm or leg?
Did these symptoms begin after a stroke, head injury, infection, or major illness?
Are you taking, or have you recently taken, medicines such as antipsychotics, metoclopramide, or prochlorperazine?
Have you ever been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease or another movement disorder?
Have Parkinson’s medications such as levodopa clearly improved your slowness or stiffness?
Has anyone in your close family had Parkinson’s disease or a similar movement disorder?
